title: Identifying Critical Fortification Node Sets for Kill-Web Mission Paths via Minimum Node-Cut Optimization
content: Kill-web absorption resilience depends on whether directed mission paths remain available after disruption. This study addresses how to allocate a limited fortification budget to mission-function nodes so that an adaptive interdictor must incur the greatest possible cost to disconnect all valid mission paths. We formulate Mission-Path Cut Fortification ( MPCF), which maximizes the post-fortification minimum node-cut cost. Node-capacity splitting converts the interdiction response for a fixed fortification set into an equivalent maximum-flow minimum-cut problem. A compact mixed-integer linear program provides the primary exact solution, and an independent cut-generation formulation cross-checks the optimum in cut space. Across 135 graph-budget pairs from 45 prespecified synthetic networks, the mean optimality gaps of MPCF-Greedy and PathFrequency are 2.76% and 9.50%, respectively. Across 810 combinations under six role-composition profiles, the two exact formulations obtain identical objective values; MPCF-Greedy has a mean gap of 1.98%, whereas the best non-MPCF method under each profile has a mean gap of 8.11%–10.12%. Exact optimization also agrees with exhaustive enumeration on 72 small fortification instances and 72 capacity-interdiction instances, and cut-space verification agrees on 30 public-network instances. These results show that mission-path fortification benefits from joint optimization of the protected node set and the adaptive minimum-cut response.
